title: (No AI) Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/alphagenome-atlas-cover__background.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

A graphic representing Google’s AlphaGenome Atlas. | Image: Google

Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease - and point the way to new treatments.

AlphaGenome 2 is the successor to DeepMind's genome-predicting AI model AlphaGenome, which was [released last year](https://deepmind.google/blog/alphagenome-ai-for-better-understanding-the-genome/). title: (No AI) Adobe’s AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters
author: Jess Weatherbed
content:
![Project Screen Test previewed at Adobe Max 2026.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/Adobe-Project-Screen-Test.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Project Screen Test lets you talk with AI-generated characters to shape their personality. | Image: Adobe

Some of the most impressive tech that Adobe showcases at its annual Max conference each year is the experimental features it's developing, and the latest of those tools are being announced today: they can transform images into explorable 3D scenes, design AI characters by talking to them, and turn photo editing into a copy/paste process.

The first (and weirdest, in my opinion) is Project Screen Test, which is designed to make AI-generated characters easier to develop and use for video content.
